findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: Inspector found Tuna salad, made in house, at 51F when temperature was taken with a probe thermometer. The tuna salad was constructed and put to cool at 8am today. The probe temperature was taken at 2:15 pm. The tuna has been in the temperature danger zone for 6 hours and 15 minutes. The tuna salad will be discarded. The tuna salad is double panned in plastic with a tight fitting lid. Inspector suggests putting tuna in the walk in freezer to cool after it is constructed. Stir tuna salad in order to help remove heat from the salad. 5 lbs of tuna salad was discarded in the garbage. Take care to use effective cooling techniques such as covering lightly, single panning or placing in an environment that is cold enough to remove the heat from the product. The hang thermometer is reading 43F. The unit has been open on top for the lunch service period and appears to be going through a defrost cycle. These factors add up when cooling. Place tuna in a cooling unit when cooling not a make table. 

(A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.comment:
6-403.11: Provide suitable location for storage of employee drinks. This location shall be low and way from food for sale to the public. 

(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed employee restocking single use cups to touch the inside of the cups. Take care to maintain the food contact and lip contact surfaces of single use articles free of potential contamination. Employee was coached at time of inspection. Violation is considered corrected on site. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no copies of food handler’s licenses at the facility. PIC was able to show the Inspector his license on his phone. Discussed with PIC. Create a public health folder/binder with all necessary documentation including copies of all employee’s food handler licenses. Employees should have a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 9/21/22 and on 5/4/21. The manager said that they had a binder but that the corporation just took it and put everything on the computer. He has to get the binder from the corporate office. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Observed the manager on duty to only be a food handler, not a certified food protection manager. It appears there is only one currently for the facility (main manager). The facility will need at least 1 more CFPM, if not 2 more in order to have a certified food protection manager available during all operational hours. Manager on duty was unaware of paperwork needed by SCDPH and Inspector helped him find the necessary paperwork in the filing cabinet. The public health paperwork and licenses should be readily available at any point in time. The file has not been updated with copies of food handler’s licenses and CFPM licenses, employee health reporting agreements, Norovirus illness clean-up policy, etc. When prompted about test strips, manager on duty has never seen them at the facility (therefore, test strips are not being routinely used to check sanitizer concentrations). When prompted about sani bucket/spray bottle process, manager on duty stated they use soap and water on food-contact surfaces, sometime dipping rags within the, “sanitize”, basin of the 3 compartment sink and cleaning. The facility needs a set rule on how to properly wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces. All staff should be made aware. Test strips should be used to check concentrations. Facility is utilizing quaternary ammonium - 200 to 400 ppm, change sanitizer every 4-6 hours to keep concentration appropriate. Inspector will follow-up on 10/3/22.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed both employee’s to be food handler certified, not a food protection manager. A CFPM must be present during all operational hours. Ensure the facility has 2-3 additional people who are certified food protection manager’s. Discussed with PIC. Provided informational page for training and exam.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements for any staff at the facility. PIC could not verify information regarding employee’s reporting health diseases that are transmissible through food. Provided blank copy of SCDPH’s employee health reporting agreement. PIC could not provide proof that Jimmy John’s as a corporation has a policy that is reviewed and signed as a part of onboarding. Either have current employee read and sign the document and obtain proof this step is completed during new hire onboarding through the Jimmy John’s system. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 1/8/20 and 5/4/21. Inspector will follow-up on 10/3/22.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

(REPEAT) Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy or bodily fluid clean-up kit. PIC indicated there is bleach at the facility to perform procedure. Provided copy of the Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Inspector suggested hanging the policy near the mop area. Discussed with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 1/8/20 and 5/4/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed no hand washing before employee donned glove to engage in food preparation activities. Discussed with PIC/employee. Proper hand washing should occur before engaging in food service. Ensure to wash hands with soap, hot water, and dry hands with a paper towel. Ensure a barrier to used to turn off faucet handles such as a paper towel in order not to re-contaminate hands. Discussed with PIC. COS. Poor/inadequate hand washing is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/8/20 and 5/4/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed one of the prep coolers to be broken. No food items were in the prep cooler. Temperature was ~68F both on the top and bottom of the prep cooler. PIC stated the cooler has been out several weeks. Facility is having difficulties obtaining a technician to repair the prep cooler. Despite this is a core (C) violation, Inspector will follow-up in ten days, 10/3/22, to see if the cooler has been repaired. Facility is only operating with one prep cooler and makes a high volume of food.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no working sanitization bucket upon inspection. Discussed with PIC. Upon questioning, it was noted that facility is not regularly sanitizing with a sani bucket or spray bottle. Soap and water are used to sanitize food-contact surfaces or rags dipped in the quaternary ammonium at the 3 compartment sink. In-use rags should be in their own sani bucket with quaternary ammonium. Spray bottles of sanitizer may be used if the spray bottle is labeled, “sanitizer”, and paper towels are utilized to wipe surfaces. Ensure to used test strips to check concentration and change buckets/spray bottles every 4-6 hours to maintain appropriate concentration. Quaternary ammonium: 200-400 ppm. COS. Provided sanitization log due to lack of awareness in importance of sanitizer use.

(D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
